name: Central Kamakura and Komachi-dori
tagline: Lively heart around the main station
description: The bustling core around Kamakura Station, where Komachi-dori's shops and snacks lead to the grand Tsurugaoka Hachimangu shrine. It is the most convenient base, with trains, cafes, restaurants and services all within easy walking distance.
bestFor: Nomads who want walkable amenities, fast Tokyo trains and everyday convenience
pros: Best transport links to Tokyo and Yokohama
Plenty of cafes, shops and restaurants

name: Hase
tagline: Great Buddha, temples and the beach
description: A relaxed coastal district home to the Great Buddha at Kotoku-in and the hydrangea-famed Hase-dera, with the beach a short walk away. The Enoden line connects it easily to the centre and along the coast.
bestFor: Those wanting temples, sea air and a quieter, scenic daily base
pros: Close to beach and major temples

name: Kita-Kamakura
description: A tranquil, leafy area north of the centre known for serene Zen temples such as Engaku-ji and Kencho-ji. It feels rural and meditative, with its own station one stop up the JR line toward Tokyo.
bestFor: Focused remote workers craving calm, greenery and temple tranquillity nearby
pros: Own station on the Tokyo line

name: Shichirigahara and Enoshima direction
description: The scenic coastal stretch west toward Enoshima, following the Enoden line past Shichirigahara's surf beaches and sea views. It suits those drawn to the ocean, sunsets over Mount Fuji on clear days and a laid-back beach lifestyle.
bestFor: Surfers and beach lovers wanting coastal living with rail access to town
